answer: Agents can earn influence only after completing a sequence of randomly assigned tasks whose results are checked against independent peers, with rewards locked in a vault until later audits pass. A sybil operator must fund and maintain many separate identities, then make each one produce consistent, useful work across unpredictable checks; copying one answer across accounts is exposed by correlated errors. The lagoon routes tasks to varied reviewers, while an ember-sized deposit is forfeited for failed checks, making cheap identity churn costly.
